figures.title: Operating empty mass vs published
figures.caption: Across 11 aircraft the mean absolute OEW error is 4.1 % (median 0.9 %); 8 of 11 are within 5 %. The B747-400 (+13.8 %) is a known over-prediction; C919 and A400M references are secondary or unspecified.
figures.alt: Parity plot and signed-error bars of modelled versus published operating empty mass for 11 aircraft.

figures.title: Error by quantity and aircraft
figures.caption: Signed errors for OEW, range (three payload-range corners and an advertised-payload point), take-off and landing field length and cruise L/D on the 11 real aircraft. Green is within 5 %, red beyond 10 %. n/a means no reference was found.
figures.alt: Heat table of signed percentage errors by aircraft and quantity.

figures.title: Range vs published values
figures.caption: Range corners differ from published values by 7.0 % (max payload), 4.6 % (MTOW, max fuel) and 8.1 % (ferry) on average, mean absolute. Most errors are positive. The C919 advertised range is a weak reference.
figures.alt: Grouped bars of range error at maximum payload, at MTOW, at ferry condition and at an advertised payload.

figures.title: Field lengths vs published values
figures.caption: Take-off field length is 11.3 % and landing field length 27.6 % from published values on average. Landing is over-predicted on every aircraft and is the weakest result.
figures.alt: Grouped bars of take-off and landing field length error for nine aircraft.

figures.title: What the comparisons actually test
figures.caption: Of 105 scored contract rows, 68 compare a registered input (data entry) and only 37 are independent model outputs, 33 of them within tolerance.
figures.alt: Stacked bars of contract rows by status per aircraft, separating registered inputs from model outputs.
